title: Constructibility of integral geometric fibres of a smooth algebraic space
statement:
Work with schemes [def-pc-scheme] and algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Smoothness and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Finite presentation means local finite presentation, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness; quasi-compactness means that affine scheme tests have quasi-compact inverse images, and quasi-separatedness means that the diagonal is quasi-compact. Separatedness means that the representable diagonal is a closed immersion on every scheme test. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Let $B$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning a quasi-compact locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], and let $f:X\to B$ be a smooth separated morphism of finite presentation from an algebraic space. A geometric fibre at $b\in B$ is $X_{\bar b}=X\times_B\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(b)}$, using an algebraic closure of the residue field [def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. It is integral if it is nonempty, reduced and irreducible, with its atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Then
$$E_f=\{b\in |B|:X_{\bar b}\text{ is integral}\}$$
is a constructible subset [def-weil-constructible-subset], independent of the chosen algebraic closures. For every morphism of schemes $h:B'\to B$, with no Noetherian assumption on $B'$, the corresponding locus for $f':X\times_BB'\to B'$ is exactly $h^{-1}(E_f)$. No properness, group structure or nonempty-fibre assumption on $f$ is imposed.

source.place: Agent-formulated algebraic-space extension of Tag 055B (lemma-nr-geom-irreducible-components-constructible), using smooth etale presentations and the finite component incidence relation; Tag 0E0A (spaces-more-morphisms lemma-geometrically-reduced-constructible) supplies the reduced-fibre counterpart. This is not a claim that 055B itself has algebraic-space sources. Constructibility is in the sense of topology.tex Tag 005G.

proof.text: Choose an affine surjective etale atlas $p:U\to X$ by [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas] and put $R=U\times_XU$, with projections $s,t$. The base is quasi-compact and $f$ is quasi-compact, so $X$ is quasi-compact. Smoothness tested on etale charts makes $U\to B$ locally finitely presented. Since $U$ is affine and $B$ is quasi-separated, being locally Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] makes $U\to B$ finitely presented, hence finite type; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $U$ Noetherian. Every etale scheme chart of $X$ is locally of finite type over the locally Noetherian $B$, hence locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth]; $X$ is quasi-separated by the assumed finite presentation and separatedness, so [lem-sfb-noetherian-affine-atlas-relation] applies: $R$ is a Noetherian scheme. Its maps to $U$ are etale, hence locally finitely presented, so $R\to B$ is locally finitely presented by [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition]. Quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of the Noetherian $R$ [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] and the same permanence lemma make $R\to B$ finitely presented. By [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover] the point map of $p$ is an open continuous quotient surjection. The presentation and all its etale surjections persist after base change by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers].

source.place: Atlas preparation for the algebraic-space extension of the finite component argument; spaces-properties.tex Tags 03H6, 03BX; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03XQ.

proof.text: For any algebraically closed geometric point of $B$, let $Y$ denote its fibre and $V$ the pulled-back atlas. It is smooth by [lem-sfb-space-smooth-surjective-fppf-locality], so $V$ is a smooth finite-type scheme over that field. By [lem-trf-smooth-geometrically-normal], $V$ is normal and reduced. It has finitely many irreducible components by [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-irreducible-components] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]; applying [lem-a1-normal-etale-components-clopen] to $\mathrm{id}_V$ makes each component open and closed. Their images in $Y$ are nonempty irreducible open subsets by continuity and openness of the atlas [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]. Reducedness of $Y$ is the etale-chart condition that its chart local rings are reduced, which holds here. Consequently $Y$ is integral if and only if it is connected: indeed a finite irreducible-open cover of a connected space has connected overlap graph, since a partition of this graph gives disjoint nonempty open unions covering the space. Overlapping irreducible open subsets have irreducible union: any nonempty open in either meets their overlap, and two such opens then meet by irreducibility. Induct along a spanning tree of the graph. Conversely every irreducible space is nonempty and connected. The empty atlas gives an empty fibre, which satisfies neither property.

source.place: Smooth-fibre reduction to connectedness: varieties.tex Tag 056T; the finite open-cover argument is written here.

proof.text: Let $b'\mapsto b$ under any $h:B'\to B$. Choose algebraic closures $K$ of $\kappa(b)$ and $K'$ of $\kappa(b')$. By [lem-weil-common-extension-fields] they embed over $\kappa(b)$ into a common field $M$. Associativity of the sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] identifies the two fibres after extension to $M$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-sepclosed-components-base-change] separately to the fibres over $K$ and $K'$: each is connected if and only if this common extension is connected. Step 2 therefore makes their integrality equivalent. Its finite-type smooth atlas exists for both fibres, independently of whether $B'$ is Noetherian, by base change of $U\to B$ and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]; smoothness persists by [lem-sfb-space-smooth-surjective-fppf-locality]. This proves the claimed equality of loci under every base change, as well as independence of the chosen algebraic closures, before proving constructibility.

Fix a nonempty irreducible closed subset $Z\subseteq |B|$. Give it the reduced induced scheme structure by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]; this is an integral Noetherian scheme with generic point $\eta$. Apply [lem-sbc-generic-components-split] to the finite-type generic fibre of $U_Z\to Z$. It gives a finite etale field extension $L/\kappa(\eta)$ over which the irreducible components $A_1,\ldots,A_n$ are geometrically irreducible. There are finitely many, by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] over the field $L$ and [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-irreducible-components]. They form a closed cover, with the empty list permitted when the fibre is empty. Apply [lem-sbc-geometric-generic-cover-model] with these supplied data. It gives an etale $g:T\to Z$, a generic point $\xi$ above $\eta$, and a finite closed cover $C_i$ of $P=U_Z\times_ZT$ whose traces on every field-extended fibre are nonempty and irreducible. Restrict $T$ to an affine neighbourhood of $\xi$. Since $Z$ is locally Noetherian, hence quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], it is finitely presented over $Z$ by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] and is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Its image $W=g(T)$ is open and contains $\eta$ by [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]. No identification of the $C_i$ with the original generic components is needed.

source.place: Tag 055G (lemma-geometrically-connected-generic-fibre), component splitting, etale model, and spreading the finite closed cover; Tag 0551.

proof.text: Set $Q=R\times_BT$, with projections $s,t:Q\to P$. Both $P$ and $Q$ are finitely presented over $T$ by step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. For each ordered pair $(i,j)$ form the closed subset $D_{ij}=s^{-1}(C_i)\cap t^{-1}(C_j)\subseteq Q$ and give it the reduced induced closed scheme structure by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. The map $D_{ij}\to T$ is quasi-compact and locally finitely presented: on Noetherian affine charts its closed immersion has finitely generated defining ideal, and it is followed by the finitely presented $Q\to T$, so the composite is locally finitely presented by [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-chevalley-constructible-image] makes its image $H_{ij}\subseteq T$ constructible. For a geometric point $\bar t$ over $t$, its fibre is nonempty exactly when $t\in H_{ij}$: a field-valued point of an ordinary fibre and the geometric field have a common extension by [lem-weil-common-extension-fields], so nonemptiness persists after the field extension; the converse follows by projection.

source.place: Finite incidence relation for the atlas: Tag 055G intersection construction, with Chevalley Tag 054J replacing its generic-flatness shrinking.

proof.text: For a geometric point $\bar t$, put a graph on $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ with edge $ij$ when $t\in H_{ij}$. It is symmetric since the relation has an inverse [lem-a1-etale-atlas-presentation]. The closed irreducible nonempty sets $(C_i)_{\bar t}$ cover $P_{\bar t}$. Their images cover $X_{\bar t}$ and are connected, by continuity of the atlas [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]. Two images meet exactly when there is an edge: two representatives of one space point agree over a common field extension, precisely the point relation defined by $P\times_XP$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers, def-a1-space-point-topology]. If the graph is nonempty and connected, the images form an intersecting connected chain along each path, so their union is connected. Conversely, if the graph has a partition into two nonempty parts with no crossing edge, the corresponding finite unions of $(C_i)_{\bar t}$ are disjoint closed sets covering $P_{\bar t}$. They are saturated for the atlas relation, since no point in the first can be related to a point in the second. The quotient topology therefore gives a partition of $X_{\bar t}$ into two nonempty closed, hence also open, subsets. Thus $X_{\bar t}$ is connected exactly when this finite graph is nonempty and connected. If $n=0$, $P$ and $X_T$ are empty and the condition is false.

source.place: Elementary finite closed-cover argument on the quotient atlas, extending the finite incidence argument of Tag 055G.

proof.text: For fixed $n>0$, graph connectedness is a finite Boolean condition on the edge sets: for every nonempty proper subset $J\subset\{1,\ldots,n\}$ require $t\in\bigcup_{i\in J,\ j\notin J}H_{ij}$. Take the intersection of these finitely many unions; for $n=1$ the empty intersection is $T$, and for $n=0$ use the empty subset. By [def-weil-constructible-subset] this defines a constructible subset $F\subseteq T$. Steps 2 and 6 identify $F$ with the integral geometric-fibre locus over $T$. Step 3 identifies it with $g^{-1}(E_f\cap Z)$. Since $g$ is surjective onto $W$, we have $g(F)=E_f\cap W$. By [lem-weil-pbc-chevalley-constructible-image], applied to the finitely presented scheme map $g:T\to Z$ with $Z$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], this is constructible in $Z$.

source.place: Tag 055B / Tag 055H finite incidence constructibility; Chevalley Tag 054J on the etale model.

proof.text: There is now a nonempty relatively open $V\subseteq Z$ which is wholly in $E_f$ or wholly outside it. Indeed $W$ contains the generic point $\eta$ of $Z$ and $E_f\cap W$ is a finite union of locally closed sets by [def-weil-constructible-subset]. If it contains $\eta$, a locally closed term containing $\eta$ has closed factor all of $Z$, hence contains an open neighbourhood of $\eta$. If it does not, the closure of each locally closed term is proper: a locally closed set dense in irreducible $Z$ is open in $Z$ and contains $\eta$. Remove these finitely many proper closed subsets from $W$. This proves the required alternative for every irreducible closed $Z$. The Noetherian scheme $B$ has a finite affine cover by Noetherian rings by its quasi-compactness and local Noetherianity. Therefore [lem-trf-noetherian-constructible-subset-criterion] applies and makes $E_f$ constructible. Together with step 3 this proves every assertion, including empty fibres and arbitrary non-Noetherian base changes.

lean.statement: theorem isConstructible_integralGeometricFibreLocus {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (B : Over S) [IsNoetherian B.left] (f : X.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj B) (hsmooth : MapToSchemeIsLocally (@Smooth) X B f) (hsep : MapToSchemeIsSeparated X B f) (hlfp : MapToSchemeIsLocally (@LocallyOfFinitePresentation) X B f) (hqc : MapIsQuasiCompact f) (hqs : MapIsQuasiCompact (pullback.diagonal f)) : Topology.IsConstructible (integralGeometricFibreLocus f) ∧ (∀ (b : B.left) (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra (B.left.residueField b) K] [IsAlgClosure (B.left.residueField b) K], IsIntegralFieldFibre f K (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (B.left.residueField b) K)) ≫ B.left.fromSpecResidueField b) ↔ b ∈ integralGeometricFibreLocus f) ∧ ∀ (B' : Over S) (h : B' ⟶ B), integralGeometricFibreLocus (Limits.pullback.snd f (yoneda.map h)) = h.left ⁻¹' integralGeometricFibreLocus f
